The Chef's Guide to EnPlace Pro

Everything you touch, screen by screen — from your first sign-in to placing a split order one-handed in the middle of service.

01

What EnPlace Pro actually does

One order screen. Every supplier you're connected to. The best price, picked for you.

You already know how this goes without EnPlace Pro: three tabs open, three logins, three carts, and a mental note that produce was cheaper at one of them last week. EnPlace Pro collapses that into a single screen.

Behind the scenes the app logs into each of your suppliers overnight, pulls down their order guides and prices, and lines up the same product across all of them. When you sit down to order, you're not shopping supplier by supplier — you're shopping by product, and every supplier who carries it shows up in a row with its price and its per-unit cost.

You pick products
Not suppliers. Type a quantity next to Spring Mix and the app has already flagged which supplier is cheapest per ounce.
It splits the order
One cart becomes one order per supplier, automatically, each with its own delivery date and its own minimum to clear.
Nothing sends itself
Every order sits in review until you press submit. The app never places an order behind your back.
Why it works this way

Prices move constantly and pack sizes are deliberately hard to compare — a 4/1 gal case and a 6/64 oz case are not the same thing. The app normalises everything to a per-unit price and marks the winner with a green BEST badge, so the comparison is done before you look at it.

What you'll be able to do by the end of this guide

  • Connect your supplier logins, including the ones that text or email you a code
  • Build a reusable order list and turn it into a real order in about two minutes
  • Read the order builder fluently — best price, per-unit, catch weight, out of stock
  • Clear supplier minimums without over-ordering
  • Do the whole thing one-handed on your phone in the middle of service
  • Fix the two things that break most often: an expired supplier session and a missed 2FA code
02

Getting in the first time

Accepting your invitation and signing in

You don't create your own account. Your owner or manager invites you, and the invitation email contains a one-time link. Clicking it lands you here:

  1. Open the invitation email and click the link. If the link says it's invalid or already used, ask for a fresh one — they expire.
  2. Fill in your first and last name, then set a password — 8 characters minimum.
  3. Press Join Rossi Restaurant Group — the button carries your restaurant group's actual name.
  4. You land straight on your dashboard with a short guided tour running.
Watch out

The email field is read-only on purpose. If there's a typo in it, you can't fix it here — the invitation itself has to be re-sent to the right address.

Signing in after that

  • Keep me signed in is ticked by default, and chefs stay signed in through 7 days of inactivity — you won't get logged out overnight or between shifts.
  • The eye icon on the password field reveals what you typed — useful on a phone with wet hands.
  • Five wrong passwords locks the account. It unlocks itself automatically after an hour — nobody has to reset it for you.
03

Connecting your first supplier

The one thing that must happen before you can order

Until at least one supplier is connected, the app has no prices to show you. That's why a brand-new chef account gently blocks most of the interface — the guided tour walks you to the same place.

Who can do this

Supplier logins live under Your avatar (top right)→Supplier Credentials. Credentials are personal: yours are yours, and you can't see your owner's.

Adding a login

Your four suppliers do not all authenticate the same way, and the form changes shape once you pick one:

SupplierWhat it asks forWhat happens on save
US FoodsUser ID onlyA verification code is sent to you
Premiere Produce OneEmail address onlyA verification code is sent to you
Chef's WarehouseEmail + passwordValidates in the background, 15–30 seconds
What Chefs WantEmail + passwordValidates in the background, 15–30 seconds
  1. Avatar menu → Supplier Credentials → Add Credential.
  2. Choose the supplier. The rest of the form only appears after you do.
  3. Enter your login. If a blue notice says the supplier uses 2FA verification only, that's expected — there is no password to enter.
  4. Press Add Credential. The credential saves as Pending and validation starts in the background.
  5. For a 2FA supplier, watch for the code and enter it (next section).
Watch out

The supplier dropdown only lists suppliers you haven't already connected at this restaurant. If it looks empty, you're already connected to everything.

04

Verification codes (2FA)

US Foods and Premiere Produce One send a code every single time

Two of your four suppliers don't use a stored password — they send a fresh code to your email or phone whenever the app needs to log in. When that happens, EnPlace Pro pops a box and waits for you.

  1. Check the email or text for the code.
  2. Type it into the box and press Verify.
  3. If it's already expired, don't retype it — go back to Supplier Credentials and press Validate on that supplier to trigger a new one.
If you get stuck

There are two places a code can be asked for and people mix them up: this full-screen modal, and a small amber Enter code box inside the supplier's card on the Supplier Credentials page. They do the same job. If the modal disappeared, look for the amber box.

The amber box says “Codes expire in ~2 minutes!” — that text is out of date. You actually get 3 to 5 minutes, and the live countdown next to it is the number to trust.

Tip

Active + Disconnected is normal for 2FA suppliers. It means your login is fine but the browser session lapsed — one Validate and a fresh code puts it right. It doesn't mean your password is wrong.

05

Your dashboard

What the app wants you to see the moment you sign in

Everything here is scoped to your restaurant — you're pinned to one, and the green badge in the top right shows which. Unlike owners and managers, you don't get a restaurant dropdown, and that's deliberate: it removes an entire category of ordering-for-the-wrong-kitchen mistakes.

PanelWhat it's telling you
Orders This WeekEvery order at your restaurant this week, whatever its status
Next DeliveryThe soonest confirmed delivery date and who it's from
Needs Price ReviewOrders where a supplier's price changed after you built the cart — these are waiting on a decision from you
Upcoming DeliveriesGrouped by day, labelled Today / Tomorrow / weekday
Order Spend This WeekMon–Sun bars; today's bar is orange
Recent OrdersYour last handful, newest first, each one clickable
Why it works this way

The counts and the bars deliberately use different rules. Orders This Week counts everything; the spend bars only count orders that actually went out. So a price-changed order you haven't resolved is in the count but not in the money. That gap is a nudge, not a bug.

What's in your top nav

  • Dashboard, Order History, Order Lists, Menu Planner
  • A magnifying glass — that's Price Check, a global search across every supplier catalog
  • The white + NEW ORDER pill — your main entry point
  • Your avatar, which hides Supplier Credentials, Product Matching and Settings
Who can do this

You won't see a Reports link. Reports are owner and manager only. Your savings still get counted — you just don't get the org-wide financial view.

06

Order lists — your reusable templates

Build the list once, reuse it every week

An order list is a saved set of products: Weekly Produce, Proteins, Dry Goods & Paper. It has no quantities and no prices — it's just the shopping list you start from, so you're not hunting through a 1,200-product catalog every Tuesday.

Tip

Lists are shared per restaurant, not per person. The list you build is the list the next chef on shift sees. Name them like someone else has to use them at 6am.

Watch out

You can see every list at your restaurant, but you can only rename, star, edit or delete the ones you created — on someone else's list the star, the delete cross and the Edit buttons simply aren't there, and only the green Order button remains. Your owner can edit any of them.

Building a list

  1. New Order List → give it a name and an optional description.
  2. On the list page, use the Search products to add... box and press Add on what you want.
  3. Remove takes something back off.
  4. Done Adding Items when you're finished — there's no separate save.
Watch out

The products you can add come from your matched list — the catalog where the same item has been lined up across suppliers. If the panel says No matched list found, product matching hasn't been set up for your restaurant yet, and your owner needs to do that first.

Two buttons that are easy to miss

Refresh Recent Orders (top of the Order Lists page) reaches out to each connected supplier and pulls in what you've actually ordered there recently, into Recent Orders lists. It's the fastest way to seed a new account with real products.

The star on a card marks a favourite, which pins it to the front of both this page and the New Order screen.

07

Starting an order

Pick what you're ordering from

Press + NEW ORDER and you get one decision to make: start from a saved list, or start from the whole matched catalog.

Choose thisWhen
An order listYour normal weekly order. The builder opens with that list's products pinned to the top, and everything else still reachable underneath.
The full matched listYou're ordering something unusual, or building from scratch. No list section — just the catalog, grouped by category.
If you get stuck

If a list shows grey text saying No matched list available instead of a green button, the list itself is fine — the restaurant has no matched catalog behind it. That's a product matching job for your owner, not something you can fix from this screen.

08

The order builder

The screen you'll spend the most time in — worth reading slowly

This is the heart of the app. Every product is a row; every supplier is a column; you type quantities and the app does the arithmetic.

Reading a row

What you seeWhat it means
BEST green pillCheapest of the available suppliers by per-unit price, not by case price
Orange ring around a cellThe supplier this line will actually be ordered from. Defaults to BEST — click any other cell to override
“compared by per-unit price”Two or more suppliers share a unit, so the comparison is apples-to-apples
CS / PC toggleThat supplier sells the item by the case and by the piece. Switching changes price, pack size and per-unit
~$359.80 and an amber estimateA catch-weight item — priced per pound, so the case total is an estimate until it's weighed
Grey No matchThat supplier hasn't been matched to this product
Grey No priceMatched, but the supplier isn't publishing a live price
Red Out of stockExcluded from the BEST comparison entirely
Small red ↑ / green ↓The price moved since the last sync

Placing the order

  1. Filter with the Search products... box, or scroll the category groups.
  2. Set quantities with − / + or by typing. The line total appears underneath the moment you do.
  3. If you want a different supplier for a line, click that supplier's cell. The orange ring moves.
  4. Watch the navy bar at the bottom: item count, running total, and one mini-meter per supplier showing how close you are to their minimum.
  5. Set the DELIVERY date.
  6. Press Create Orders.
If you get stuck

Create Orders greyed out? It needs two things: at least one item, and a delivery date. Hovering it says so. This is comfortably the number one place people stall.

Also: pressing Enter never submits — every input swallows it. You have to click the button.

Tip

Your quantities auto-save as you go. Wander off, come back tomorrow, and the cart is still there — including which supplier you picked for each line. Only actually placing the orders clears it.

Watch out

The supplier columns are only the suppliers you personally have an active credential for. If a whole price column vanishes, that supplier's login has lapsed — the product hasn't been discontinued.

09

Review and submit

One cart in, one order per supplier out

Creating orders splits your cart by supplier. Nothing has been sent yet — this screen is the last gate, and it's where minimums get enforced rather than merely displayed.

The banners, in plain English

BannerWhat to do
Blue — Verifying prices with suppliers…Wait. The app is re-checking live prices.
Amber — Some prices have changedRead the changes, then Accept All Changes or Skip Verification.
Red — Price verification failedRetry, or Skip & Submit if you're confident and in a hurry.
Red — Order minimum not metThat one supplier is blocked. Add items or drop it.
Why it works this way

A supplier under its minimum blocks only itself. Its card gets a red ring and a greyed Submit Order, and the big button at the bottom relabels to something like Submit 1 of 2 Orders. That looks like an error — it isn't. It's the app letting the good order through while it waits on the other one.

  1. Check each supplier card: delivery date, quantities, and whether it says Ready or Minimum not met.
  2. Adjust quantities right here if you need to — the minimum re-checks live.
  3. Use the yellow Quick add to reach minimum strip to close a gap in one click, if it's offered.
  4. Add a note for the supplier if you need one.
  5. Submit per supplier with Submit Order, or everything at once with the button at the bottom.
Tip

Leaving this page is safe. Everything sits in Order History as a Draft with a Return to Checkout button. Drafts expire 14 days after you last look at them.

10

The order, after you've sent it

Tracking, receiving and reordering
StatusWhat you can do
PendingEdit quantities, date and notes; submit it
ProcessingNothing — it's being placed with the supplier; the page refreshes itself
Submitted / ConfirmedMark as Received when it lands; Reorder to clone it
FailedRetry, and read the error message
Watch out

Two real quirks worth knowing:

1. There is no Cancel button on the desktop order page. Cancelling only exists on the phone, and only while an order is still pending. On desktop, an unwanted pending order gets removed with the trash icon in Order History.

2. Reorder prices at today's rates and silently drops anything discontinued — so the new total won't match the old one. Always glance over a reorder before submitting.

Why the numbers at the top don't match the list below

The three KPI cards always mean completed orders in the date range — they ignore the status filter completely. Meanwhile open work (drafts, price-changed, failed) is always pulled into the list regardless of the date range, so a three-week-old draft shows up in a seven-day window. The two numbers legitimately disagree.

Also: cancelled orders are hidden unless you explicitly filter for them.

11

The phone app is a different app

Same data, deliberately different shape

EnPlace Pro doesn't just shrink the desktop layout on a phone — it serves genuinely different screens, built for one thumb during service.

There's no top nav on a phone. Navigation is three tabs pinned to the bottom of the screen:

TabWhere it goes
HomeYour dashboard
Order (the green + button)Straight into ordering
CartYour in-progress cart, or your order history if there's nothing in flight
On your phone

The avatar circle at the top right of your dashboard holds the rest of it: Settings, Feedback, the light/dark toggle and Sign out.

Supplier Credentials is not in that menu on a phone. The only way in from mobile is the Fix button on the broken-connection alert, which only appears when something is actually broken. To add or edit a supplier login at any other time, use a laptop.

Watch out

If Order and Cart are greyed out and tapping does nothing, it's one of two things: your account still has setup to finish, or (for owners) no specific restaurant is selected. As a chef, it almost always means no supplier is connected yet.

12

Ordering from your phone

The screen designed for the middle of a shift

How it works

  1. Tap the green Order button, pick a list.
  2. Search, or tap a category chip (All, ⭐ Frequent, Dairy, Produce…).
  3. On a product card, tap the supplier's price — that adds one and turns the cell into a stepper.
  4. Tap the same cell again to increase, or use the bigger steppers in the In this order section below.
  5. Check the navy ribbon above the tab bar: per-supplier totals, minimum warnings, delivery date.
  6. Tap Review $total.
If you get stuck

A blank product list is normal. With an empty search box and the All chip selected, the mobile builder shows nothing but Search every supplier at once. It hasn't failed to load — you have to type something or pick a category chip.

Tip

The green star on a price marks the best per-unit price, same as desktop. Adding at the starred price gives you a little savings animation — that's the app telling you it worked.

The per-cell steppers are tiny. The ones in In this order at the bottom are much bigger and do the same job — use those when your hands are busy.

The mobile-only superpower

Mobile search reaches the full supplier catalog, not just your matched list — the Everything else section. Tap the green + and the item drops into your order immediately. Desktop has no equivalent inside the builder.

Watch out

Adding a catalog item this way changes the shared matched list and flags it for your owner or manager to review. It's not a private shortcut — it's a mid-shift grab that someone will price-check later. That's the intended workflow, so use it freely, just know it's visible.

13

Your cart, and placing the order

All-or-nothing on mobile

The mobile cart is deliberately simpler than desktop review: no notes, no SKUs, no per-line delete. You adjust quantities, set a delivery date per order, and place them.

Watch out

Mobile is all-or-nothing. There's one Place 2 Orders button and no per-supplier submit. If any supplier is under its minimum, or any order is missing a delivery date, that button is disabled, and nothing explains why when you tap it. The reason is written in red in the sticky footer, directly under the Place button.

Tip

Cancel Order is a mobile-only feature and only appears while an order is still pending. It's a two-tap confirm: the first tap changes the label to Tap again to cancel.

Why it works this way

The same order can read 9 items on your phone and 4 items on desktop. Mobile counts total quantity; desktop counts the number of product lines. Both are right.

14

Price Check

A fast price lookup without leaving what you're doing

The magnifying glass in the top nav opens a search across every supplier catalog you're connected to — not just your order guide. Use it when someone asks what something costs, or when you need to add an off-list item to a list.

  • Type at least three characters.
  • Pick a destination list in Add to:, then press Add on a result.
  • The green or red dot is stock status.
  • Esc or clicking the backdrop closes it.
Watch out

Price Check won't render at all if your restaurant context is missing, and it's owner/chef only — managers don't get the icon.

15

Product matching

Why the same product from four suppliers becomes one row

Matching is what makes price comparison possible: it decides that US Foods Spring Mix 3/2 LB and Chef's Warehouse Spring Mix 6/1 LB are the same thing. As a chef you can see it, and at your own restaurant you can fix it.

Click any product's left cell to open the editor, where you can rename the item, choose which supplier's photo represents it, reassign a supplier's product, or remove the line.

Who can do this

If the list carries a purple Org-Wide badge it is read-only for everyone, including your owner, until it's demoted. That's not a permissions problem with your account.

Tip

A bad match shows up as a nonsense price comparison — a 25 lb case next to a 5 lb case. If you spot one, open the row and fix the assignment. It stays fixed, permanently, even when new suppliers get added later.

16

Menu Planner

Costing an event menu against real supplier prices

The Menu Planner is a chat with an AI that knows your suppliers' actual catalog and prices. Describe an event and it produces a costed menu — course by course, ingredient by ingredient, with a real price attached to each line.

  1. New Event Plan — this drops you straight into the conversation.
  2. Describe the event: covers, cuisine, budget per cover, dietary constraints.
  3. Refine by chatting. Ask it to swap a course, cut cost, or change a wine pairing.
  4. Check the Cost Summary — total, per cover, versus budget, and how many ingredients actually matched.
  5. Build Order turns the ingredient list into pending orders plus a saved order list.
Watch out

Build Order only appears once a menu has actually been generated, and it creates pending orders — you still go through the normal review and submit. Check the per-supplier minimums in the summary first; an event menu often leaves one supplier well short.

Tip

Plans are personal — your owner can't see yours. The monthly quota is shared, though, and deleting a plan doesn't give the slot back.

17

When something stops working

The two failures that account for almost everything

1. A supplier connection has broken

While a supplier is in this state, its prices don't update and you can't order from it — which on the builder looks like an entire price column quietly disappearing.

MessageWhat it means
Session expired — please re-validateNormal for 2FA suppliers. Validate and enter a fresh code.
Credentials are no longer validYour password changed at the supplier. Edit the credential.
Account on holdThe supplier put your account on hold. Call them — the app can't fix this.
Validation failedRead the detail on the row; often a temporary supplier-side outage.
  1. Press Re-validate → on the alert — on a phone the same button is labelled Fix. Either way it takes you to Supplier Credentials.
  2. Press Validate on that supplier's card.
  3. For a 2FA supplier, enter the code that arrives. For a password supplier, re-enter the password if it's changed.
  4. The alert disappears by itself once it succeeds — there's nothing to dismiss.

2. A price changed after you built the cart

This surfaces as Needs Price Review on your dashboard and an amber banner on the review screen. Read what moved, then either Accept All Changes and carry on, or go back and switch that line to a different supplier.

If you get stuck

A price column is missing. Nine times out of ten it's an expired credential, not a discontinued product. Check Supplier Credentials before you go hunting through the catalog.

You can't reach Supplier Credentials or Product Matching. Both need a specific restaurant in context. As a chef you're pinned to one, so this is rare — but if it happens, sign out and back in.

18

Your account settings

Small screen, one big gotcha
Watch out

Every change needs your current password — including just fixing a typo in your first name. That's the single most common failed save on this screen.

  • Nothing organizational lives here: not your role, not your restaurant, not your supplier logins.
  • Delete my account removes you, not the organization. It can't be undone.
  • The theme toggle (Light / Dark / System) is in the avatar menu, not here.
Click anywhere or press Esc to close
